titre: People will start treating you differently when you master these 7 laws of quiet elegance #elegance #etiquette #socialskills #smartgirl #selfimprovement
notes: Schéma laws-of-influence (62da2c91 r 6,62 ; 407f4a4f r 5,30 sur 6 passages). Accroches écrites : « People will start treating you differently when you master these 7 laws of quiet elegance » (retenue : le gagnant mot pour mot, avec une loi précise et élégante, pas une « loi de la vie » vague qui fait flop), « The unspoken laws of a cultured woman » (écartée : plus loin du gabarit), « 10 laws of graceful conversation » (écartée : sans la promesse de changement de statut). Title Case comme @richgirlacadmy_1, sans émojis (ils ne passent pas au rendu). Sept lois de bonnes manières, aucune manipulation, aucune reprise des 24 lois des deux inspirations : le détail retenu, citer qui a eu l'idée, sortir d'une conversation avec élégance, ouvrir le cercle, tenir les petites promesses, une meilleure question que « what do you do? », avoir toujours une histoire à raconter. Sophia sur la dernière loi, en « I », avec la formule « a micro-learning app like the Sophia app ». Images de la banque du label, sans texte lisible (28a1b924, 1c986587, 31a6567b écartées) ; slide Sophia sur une bougie et un vase, sans personne (4780aef4 écartée : filigrane).

slides.texte_overlay:
People will start treating
you differently when you
master these 7 laws
of quiet elegance.

1. The Law of the
Remembered Detail
Remember one small thing
someone told you and ask
about it next time. People
never forget feeling
remembered.

2. The Law of
Generous Credit
When an idea works, name
the person who had it.
Giving credit costs nothing
and earns lasting trust.

3. The Law of the
Graceful Exit
Never vanish mid-sentence.
Leave with a warm line:
"I loved hearing about
your trip. Enjoy the
evening."

4. The Law of the
Open Circle
When someone joins your
group, step back to make
room and tell them in one
line what you were
talking about.

5. The Law of the
Kept Word
The book you said you'd
lend, the message you said
you'd send. Small promises
kept are the most
underrated elegance.

6. The Law of the
Better Question
Skip "what do you do?"
Ask "what has been keeping
you busy lately?" People
answer with what they love.

7. The Law of the
Full Mind
Always have a story to tell:
a painting, a piece of
history, a strange fact.
Feed your mind a little
every day.
